candidates.name: options-dataset-hist
candidates.what_it_holds: README claims historical options data for SPY/IWM/QQQ, Jan 2008-Dec 2025, 53M+ contracts with Greeks/IV/microstructure, in SQLite (.db.zst) and partitioned Parquet. VERIFIED via gh api: repo is only 1886 KB total; data/spy_options.db.zst, iwm_options.db.zst, qqq_options.db.zst are each ~134-135 bytes (git-lfs pointer stubs, not real data); data/parquet_spy, parquet_iwm, parquet_qqq are empty (0-byte) directories; no GitHub releases with assets. The referenced upstream (github.com/philippdubach/historic-options-dataset) returns 404 (deleted/renamed). This looks like an unpopulated/placeholder or fork of a dead repo despite a convincing description.
candidates.why_useful: Would be a strong general options/IV methodology dataset (index ETF proxies for IV term structure and event-window construction) if real, but currently non-functional — no usable bytes behind the claim.
candidates.size_hint: repo 1.9MB total; data files are ~134-byte stubs; parquet dirs empty

candidates.name: cutemarkets-cookbook
candidates.what_it_holds: Runnable Python/TypeScript recipes for the CuteMarkets commercial options-data API, organized by workflow: options-chain scanners, historical contract reconstruction, an explicit 'earnings-implied-move' recipe, and quote-quality checks. VERIFIED via README: requires signup and a paid API key at cutemarkets.com; no data or precomputed results are committed in the repo itself — it is documentation for calling a paid live API.
candidates.why_useful: The earnings-implied-move recipe (straddle-based) is a directly reusable formula/method for building our own ABNB 5-Nov implied-move calculator once fed our existing Yahoo/Bloomberg options chain, even without the paid API subscription.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: we already hold current Yahoo options chains + a licensed Bloomberg options workbook; this only supplies a formula, not new data

candidates.name: cutemarkets-typescript
candidates.what_it_holds: TypeScript SDK for CuteMarkets' real-time and historical options data API (chains, contracts, quotes, trades, aggregates), with example scanners and earnings workflows. 79 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Same family as the cookbook above; a typed client if the team ever pays for the underlying commercial feed. On its own, no committed data.

candidates.name: Earnings-Implied-Move-Mispricing
candidates.what_it_holds: A research framework (per description) studying earnings-implied-move mispricing: option straddle prices, realized post-earnings moves, volatility features, and event history; models predicted cross-sectional edge and evaluates long-short strategies on under/overpriced earnings volatility. No stars yet, single contributor, updated 14 Jun 2026 — likely a student/independent project; not yet inspected for whether raw data is committed or pulled live.
candidates.why_useful: Directly on-theme methodology for constructing an ABNB earnings-implied-move / vol-crush estimator ahead of the 5 Nov print (straddle price vs realized move), which is exactly the reverse-DCF/market-implied-move work already underway (see reverse-dcf-run memory note) — worth a closer read for the modeling approach even if the underlying tickers are not ABNB.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps in spirit with our own market-implied reverse-DCF work (12-13 Sep 2026, docs/reverse_dcf/SYNTHESIS.md) which already derived a 12M implied-move sd of 9.5% for the 5 Nov print; this repo's method could be a cross-check, not a new number

candidates.name: Earnings-implied-move-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Python analysis comparing options-implied vs actual realized earnings moves for Nifty 50 (Indian) stocks. 0 stars, updated 16 Mar 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Same implied-vs-realized-move methodology as above, applicable in principle to ABNB once fed US options chain + earnings-date realized moves, but built and tested only on Indian large caps so the code likely needs adaptation (different exchange conventions, expiry cycles).

candidates.name: options-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Described as a 'historical options data store for backtesting and analysis'; MIT licensed, updated 15 Jul 2026, 1 star. Not yet inspected for whether it commits actual chain data or is a scraper/ETL scaffold pointing at a paid feed (common pattern in this search).
candidates.why_useful: Possible general-purpose options-chain storage/ETL tool that could be pointed at ABNB's own option chain (we already pull current Yahoo chains) to build a rolling historical archive ourselves, which we do not currently have (our options data is 'current' only, not a time series).

candidates.name: polygonData
candidates.what_it_holds: Scripts issuing historical-options-data requests against the Polygon.io API. 27 stars, updated 30 Mar 2026. Polygon.io's historical options endpoints require a paid tier; no data files committed, this is a client only.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made query pattern if the team later pays for Polygon's options history to build an ABNB IV/skew time series around past prints; not usable free.

candidates.name: option-data-collector
candidates.what_it_holds: Queries for downloading historical option data from OptionMetrics and CBOE. 5 stars, updated 30 Mar 2026. OptionMetrics is a paid academic/institutional dataset (like WRDS); CBOE side may include some free sample endpoints.
candidates.why_useful: Only useful if the team or a partnering university library has OptionMetrics/WRDS access; otherwise not free. Worth flagging in case UF library provides WRDS/OptionMetrics access for the options-implied-move work.

notes: Six gh search repos calls used (budget cap). Two of six searches ('post earnings announcement drift dataset', 'implied volatility term structure dataset') returned zero hits, and two more ('CBOE options historical', 'ORATS OR earnings volatility crush') also returned zero — gh search repos appears not to support boolean OR syntax, so the ORATS query effectively searched a garbled literal string; a follow-on scout should retry 'ORATS' and 'earnings volatility crush' as separate single-phrase queries, and also try 'PEAD dataset', 'CBOE DataShop sample', 'IV surface dataset github', 'straddle earnings backtest' with fresh budget. The single most interesting hit (SaidBahaDev/options-dataset-hist, 53M SPY/IWM/QQQ option contracts 2008-2025) was verified via gh api to be essentially empty — git-lfs pointer stubs of ~134 bytes and empty parquet directories, no release assets, and its stated upstream (philippdubach/historic-options-dataset) 404s — a caution that GitHub descriptions in this space are frequently aspirational/AI-generated rather than real; treat any options-data repo claim as unverified until `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/<path>` shows nonzero file sizes or a release with assets. No repo found in this pass holds free, real, committed historical single-name option-chain data (CBOE DataShop-style, ORATS-like) or a genuine free IV-term-structure or earnings-drift dataset; everything found is either (a) a client/SDK for a paid API (CuteMarkets, Polygon.io, OptionMetrics) or (b) a small student implied-move-vs-realized-move analysis script (Nifty 50 or unspecified US names) that is a reusable METHOD, not a data source. This means gap #17's 'earnings-implied-move estimators' is best filled by adapting the straddle-price methodology from unniananya/Earnings-Implied-Move-Mispricing or pratham-1230's Nifty analysis and applying it to ABNB's own current Yahoo/Bloomberg options chain around the 5 Nov print, rather than importing any external historical dataset — consistent with the existing reverse-DCF market-implied work already in the repo (docs/reverse_dcf/SYNTHESIS.md, 12M sd 9.5%). Recommend a future scout specifically target 'CBOE DataShop', 'WRDS options', 'ivolatility github', and 'earnings volatility crush python' with a fresh 6-call budget, and also check for academic replication packages tied to PEAD papers (Bernard-Thomas style) which often commit small CRSP-derived event-study CSVs.
